Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

entry = rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC horizontal bars crossed by vertical gaps', path='arc-patterns', global_=True, content='''A useful ARC pattern: sparse horizontal colored bars contain single-cell gaps aligned with a vertical column, while colored vertical stubs appear at the bottom of those columns. Reconstruct each vertical column by extending the horizontal bar colors through the gaps and blank spaces between successive horizontal-bar crossings. For each column, ordered crossings from top to bottom partition vertical space: the topmost crossing color extends from the top edge to that row; each next crossing color fills from just below the prior crossing through its own row. The bottom stub color extends upward through the blank gap below the last crossing, and remains unchanged. Fill only those vertical columns; preserve other zeros and horizontal shapes. In task-44656973 example: c3 crossings at rows 2/6/11 with colors 2/3/4 and bottom stub 6 at rows13-14, yielding c3=2 at rows0-2, 3 at 3-6, 4 at 7-11, 6 at 12-14. c8 crossings rows3/8/11 colors5/9/4, bottom stub8 at r14, yielding segments r0-3=5, r4-8=9, r9-11=4, r12-14=8. A single demo showed the same rule with one crossing: extend crossing color up to top, bottom-stub color upward to crossing. Treat as a pattern clue, not universal unless layout supports it.''')
